transcription: Main article text only (site banner, menus, the 'On this page:' sidenav, breadcrumbs, the feedback form and footer removed); H1 title line from the page's own H1. The figure (labelled airliner drawing) is not part of the text: it is stored separately as figure nasa-grc-airplane-parts-1; the page gives it no caption (alt text 'Diagram of airplane parts', not kept), and the right-aligned 'NASA-Glenn-Airplane-Parts' download link under it (a PDF of the figure) is removed. purpose: library: the parts of an airliner and what each does — wings generating most of the lift (winglets reduce drag; turbine engines under the wings provide thrust to overcome drag); the tail's fixed horizontal stabilizer (prevents pitch) and vertical stabilizer (prevents yaw), and the canard of the Wright aircraft; the hinged control surfaces — rudder (tail left/right), elevator (tail up/down), aileron (roll) and spoilers (disrupt the flow, decrease lift, roll and slow the plane); flaps and slats deployed at takeoff and landing; the fuselage holding the pieces together, with the cockpit at the front and passengers, cargo and sometimes fuel behind; and other configurations (pusher propellers, buried jet engines, stabilators). Carries figure nasa-grc-airplane-parts-1 (labelled airliner drawing, NASA insignia removed) for label the diagram; also fits a compare table of part vs function and quiz cards with predict-then-reveal.
